mood_contract: Generosity: the student starts from one teammate's job, not a rollout obligation, and leaves with one name and one small move. Sharing never reads as governance or as a correction of the reader.

intended_learnings.text: Start from the teammate's job, not from your agent; the outcome statement is the contract a candidate must move.
You can share the context, a skill, the output (push) or an interface (pull); never the whole agent.
Context, boundaries and checks copy; the person who answers for what the agent does does not travel inside a folder.
Access is a switch that completes in a minute; absorption happens in other people's weeks, at their pace, for their reasons.
Ask what would have to be true for the teammate to switch from their current solution, then test those assumptions.
A missing name in the people plan is a finding; the next move is one named person and one tested assumption.

pad: Sharing AI tools across a team is a rapidly evolving area, and organisations of every size are working out how best to approach it. It is important to involve the right stakeholders early, to follow best practices, and to keep iterating as the landscape changes.

Industry analysts expect agent adoption to accelerate significantly over the coming years, which makes change management all the more important. Leading companies are investing in enablement programmes, champions networks and training.

Remember that adoption is everyone's responsibility. Clear communication, strong sponsorship and regular follow-up remain the foundation, and agents are simply one more area where those principles apply.
